title: Agree the scope, sponsor and decision the strategy supports
summary: A strategy needs a clear question, an owner and someone senior who will act on it. Agree these first, so the work leads to a decision rather than a document.

beginner: Write down the question the strategy must answer, in one sentence.
Name the sponsor: the senior person who will decide and back it.
Agree what is in scope and what is not, such as which products or markets.
Agree when the decision is needed and who must be involved.
Share this on one page and get the sponsor to agree it.
intermediate: Frame the strategy around a real decision, such as where to invest next year.
Agree decision rights: who decides, who advises and who is told.
Set a timebox so the work doesn't drift.
experienced: Link the mandate to company goals and the budget cycle.
Spot conflicting mandates across teams and resolve them early.
Agree how the strategy will be reviewed and refreshed.

canDelegateTo.task: Set up the timeline and meetings

toolExamples.confluence: Write the one-page mandate and link it from the strategy space.
toolExamples.notion: Keep the mandate as the first page of the strategy workspace.

pitfalls: A question too broad to answer

sources.title: The perils of bad strategy (Richard Rumelt, McKinsey Quarterly)
